outcome: Refine visual storytelling and routine flow in the existing Long Return opening into one continuous map-led adventure; implement, verify, and deploy without expanding the concept.
authorizedScope: Nick agreed to focus on the first two deficiencies before adding content, requested this goal, and previously authorized experiments, fixes, verification, and deployment without repeated check-ins. Existing encounters, routes, mechanics, creature facts, and platform rules stay outside expansion scope. Technical evidence does not establish subjective endorsement.

criteria.expectation: One persistent map shows scouting, reporting, return, route traversal, discovered hazards, and physical crossing consequences.
criteria.assessment: Inspected automatic remote-report climbing and isolated-scout return/intake runs. The same map persists through both decisions and distinct landings; brine remains hidden until communicated or encountered. Responsive checks at 320x568, 390x600, 820x900, 1280x720, and 1600x1000; 2519px desktop bounds were also measured.

criteria.expectation: Readable automatic narration leads into decisions without redundant report/result acknowledgement; retain earlier text, pause, skip, and meaningful choices.
criteria.assessment: Reports and crossings advance automatically into available decisions after reading time. Prior text persists, pause holds, skip remains optional, and no extra report/result acknowledgement is required. Map/account/footer bounds stayed identical through the verified runs. Reading focus is preserved; obsolete playback control focus moves to the next decision.

criteria.expectation: Preserve costs, concealed findings, techniques, commands, discoveries, field work, checkpoint resume, withdrawal, and next-room handoff.
criteria.assessment: 352 Long Return tests passed, followed by all nine final default-opening cases after the last focus adjustment. Actual paid return, intake repair, resource exchange, checkpoint resume, next-room arrival, and help/log closure inspected in the browser. Commands, techniques, warnings, signal investigation, costs, and withdrawal use existing handlers. No engine or checkpoint-format change.

criteria.expectation: Required CI passes, change merges and deploys, and the live opening is directly inspected.
criteria.assessment: Final local production build passed. PR, required CI, deployment, and live inspection remain executable.

findings.observation: Short-phone map labels and crew numbers were too small, and resources were hidden by utility styles.
findings.resolution: Labels and markers are enlarged on smaller screens with nonoverlapping crew spacing, resources explicitly retained, and a fixed reserve area. Phone panels and footer retained their recorded bounds through return and crossing.

findings.observation: A returned scout could move back ahead when the final report cleared, and automatic completion needed reading-focus preservation.
findings.resolution: Returned scouts remain with the crew; findings wait for completed return. Automatic handoff preserves account reading focus and removes focus from changing playback buttons. Final focused cases pass.

findings.observation: The implementation is local and undeployed.
findings.nextAction: Complete checks, open and attach the PR, merge through CI, and inspect the deployed opening.

findings.observation: At 320 by 568, the help close button overlapped the persistent navigation menu; clicking it opened navigation instead of closing help.
findings.resolution: Opening help and log overlays now begin below the persistent navigation and fit the viewport. Actual 320x568 help/log close clicks succeeded and restored Rules/Log focus; integration tests pass.

audit.comparison: Direct desktop and phone playthroughs against the stated opening criteria, without treating passing tests as subjective approval.
audit.regressions: Existing full-mission comparisons exercise the previous opening; new integration tests exercise the default continuous opening and next-room handoff.
audit.scopeCheck: No content catalog, route, encounter, mechanic, creature contract, or platform cutover was added.
